role: VPR image augmentation experience bank. The goal is high-quality positive augmentation for Visual Place Recognition, prioritizing place identity, geometry preservation, realistic environmental change, and realistic dynamic occlusion.

route_ratio.local_dual_balance: local and dual should stay close to 1:1 when both are visually reasonable

weather_ratio.note: Weather coverage is a dataset design target. It should guide sampling but must not override scene suitability or hard skip decisions.

global: normal street scene suitable for weather change
occlusion placement is unclear or unsafe
local: clear legal vehicle or person placement exists
weather change is unnecessary or less important
dual: clear legal vehicle or person placement exists

night.experience: highest risk for vehicle dual augmentation

vehicle.experience: Vehicle occlusion should be preferred whenever a traffic lane, curbside lane, parking bay, or roadside parking area is visible.

person.experience: Use person only when no reasonable vehicle placement exists but a sidewalk, curb, crosswalk, or roadside pavement is clear.

black_vehicle_block.note: Current pixel heuristic over-kills visually acceptable dark vehicles; keep as warning.

sign_or_storefront_color_deformation.note: Current pixel heuristic over-kills visually acceptable lighting/color changes; keep as warning.

positive_prompt: Put IC-Light global weather, photorealistic street-view, facade preservation, and no-stylization constraints within the first 77 CLIP tokens.
For LightX2V vehicle prompts, mention only vehicle attributes and legal vehicle placement.
For LightX2V person prompts, mention only pedestrian attributes and legal pedestrian placement.
Do not mix person instructions into vehicle prompts.
Do not include forbidden artifact names in the positive prompt.
negative_prompt: Put black block, blob, silhouette, pasted, floating, wall, sky, storefront deformation, and painterly/style terms only in the negative prompt.
Use no-oil-painting and no-stylization constraints for IC-Light global generations.

global_rain.target: rainy street scene, wet reflective road, overcast sky, subtle visible falling rain
global_rain.avoid: rain only shown as wet ground without atmosphere

global_snow.target: snowy street scene, light snow, realistic winter atmosphere, thin snow on sidewalks and parked cars
global_snow.avoid: heavy snow that hides place-defining facades or road geometry

global_night.target: night street scene, dim artificial street lighting, reduced saturation, controlled low-light exposure
global_night.avoid: over-dark image or changed facade/window/fence/tree structure

global_overcast.target: overcast street scene, uniform cloudy sky, soft diffuse daylight, muted contrast, no strong shadows
global_overcast.avoid: turning the scene into rain, night, or heavy fog

global_fog.target: foggy street scene, realistic dense fog with reduced long-range visibility while keeping nearby road and facade geometry readable
global_fog.avoid: fog so heavy that it hides place-defining facades, signs, lane markings, or road layout

local_vehicle.target: exactly one normal street vehicle such as car, van, bus, or taxi, wheels aligned with road perspective, natural scale, placed only on visible traffic lane, curbside lane, parking bay, or roadside parking area
local_vehicle.avoid: pure black vehicle blob, floating vehicle, vehicle on sidewalk, vehicle on wall, vehicle on sky, vehicle on building facade, oversized foreground vehicle, traffic jam, changed road layout

local_person.target: exactly one normal full-body pedestrian, natural scale, realistic clothing color, feet firmly on visible sidewalk, curb, crosswalk, or roadside pavement
local_person.avoid: edge shadow person, black silhouette, dark blob, tiny pedestrian, border pedestrian, floating person, cutout person, crowd

dual_rain_vehicle.target: rainy street scene, wet reflective road, plus one normal vehicle on a visible road lane, curb lane, or parking lane with matched rainy lighting
dual_rain_vehicle.avoid: pure black vehicle blob, wrong lane position, traffic jam, changed road layout

dual_overcast_vehicle.target: overcast street scene, soft overcast daylight, plus one normal vehicle on a visible road lane, curb lane, or parking lane
dual_overcast_vehicle.avoid: pure black vehicle blob, rain artifacts, traffic jam, changed road layout

dual_fog_vehicle.target: foggy street scene, realistic fog, plus one normal vehicle on a visible nearby lane or parking lane, with tires aligned to road perspective
dual_fog_vehicle.avoid: pure black vehicle blob, fog hiding road layout, traffic jam, changed road geometry

dual_snow_vehicle.target: snowy street scene, light snow, plus one normal vehicle on a visible lane or parking lane with tires aligned to the road perspective
dual_snow_vehicle.avoid: pure black vehicle blob, traffic jam, heavy snow hiding landmarks

dual_night_vehicle.target: night street scene plus one normal vehicle on a visible lane or curb lane with subtle realistic headlight spill
dual_night_vehicle.avoid: pure black vehicle blob, multiple new cars, traffic jam, changed lane geometry

reflection_lessons: Occluders must be real street participants, not abstract masks or edge shadows.
Prefer vehicle occlusion whenever a clear lane, curbside lane, parking bay, or roadside parking area is available.
A vehicle occluder should be a normal car, van, bus, or taxi placed on a visible road lane, curb lane, or parking lane with tires aligned to the road perspective.
A person occluder should be a full-body pedestrian walking or standing on visible sidewalk, curb, crosswalk, or road-edge pavement, with feet touching the ground plane.
Skip close-up facades, wall/window/sign/storefront fragments, sky fragments, and scenes without a valid street surface.
Use moderate occlusion; avoid heavy, massive, or extreme obstruction.
Do not include city names such as London, New York, Tokyo, Paris, or Beijing in generation prompts.
